hero.description_blurb: AOD9604 is a synthetic 16-amino-acid peptide corresponding to residues 177-191 of human growth hormone with an added N-terminal tyrosine (Tyr-hGH 177-191), listed by some suppliers as HGH Fragment 176-191 or LAT8881. Veracue supplies it as a research material for laboratory work. The most directly relevant human data come from a 24-week Phase 2B trial (Metabolic Pharmaceuticals, 2007), the largest efficacy study of AOD9604 in adults with obesity. That trial did not find a statistically significant weight-loss benefit over placebo, so this material does not establish weight loss, treatment effect or safety in people.

sections.heading: What Is AOD9604 Peptide?
body: AOD9604 is a synthetic peptide built from the tail end of human growth hormone (hGH): residues 177–191, with an extra tyrosine added at the front. One disulfide bond closes part of the chain into a loop. Metabolic Pharmaceuticals developed it in Australia as a candidate obesity drug, building on Monash University research into the C-terminal region of hGH. Later clinical protocols refer to the same peptide as LAT8881.

The name AOD9604 is sometimes used for the closely related sequence hGH Fragment 176-191. Native hGH residues 176–191 begin with phenylalanine (FLRIVQCRSVEGSCGF), while AOD9604 adds a tyrosine ahead of residues 177–191 (YLRIVQCRSVEGSCGF). Because vendors use the two names inconsistently, sequence, disulfide state, expected mass and lot-specific analytical data are the most reliable way to confirm which peptide a product actually is.

sections.heading: Molecular Identity and Specifications
body: These values describe the AOD9604 molecule itself, checked against PubChem and FDA's 2024 evaluation. They are reference data, not a result from a specific Veracue lot.

sections.heading: Why Researchers Study AOD9604
body: AOD9604 is a useful case study in isolating one part of a hormone from the rest. Growth hormone affects growth, glucose handling and fat metabolism together. The research programme behind AOD9604 asked whether a short C-terminal fragment could reproduce the fat-metabolism signal on its own.

It also has a documented, if mixed, translational record. Preclinical findings in rodents led to a full sequence of human trials and a clear efficacy result at the end. That makes it a useful reference for researchers examining how animal metabolic signals do or do not carry over to people. Its defined sequence and single disulfide bond also make it useful for method-development work, such as peptide characterisation and stability testing.

sections.heading: Mechanism and Biological Research Context
body: AOD9604's molecular target has not been established. In cell assays, it did not compete with hGH for growth-hormone-receptor binding and did not drive receptor-dependent cell growth. In human trials, serum IGF-1 did not differ from placebo. So it does not behave as a conventional GH secretagogue.

Preclinical work in obese mice found that AOD9604 raised expression of the β3-adrenergic receptor, the main lipolytic receptor in fat cells. Its chronic weight and lipolysis effects were absent in β3-AR knockout mice, though an acute rise in energy expenditure still occurred. These are mechanistic observations from specific models, not a confirmed pathway.

sections.heading: Human Clinical Research History
body: AOD9604 has a genuine human research history. Between 2001 and 2006, its developer ran six randomised, placebo-controlled trials, moving from intravenous safety studies to oral efficacy trials in adults with obesity.

rows: Well tolerated; no serious adverse events
Well tolerated; no consistent weight signal
Positive weight-loss signal reported in a conference abstract; full data never published
Oral, once daily, with diet and exercise
No statistically significant weight loss vs placebo at 12 or 24 weeks; obesity programme ended in 2007

after_table: The OPTIONS study was the decisive efficacy trial. It was the largest and longest of the six, and it directly tested weight loss against placebo. When it missed its endpoint, the developer terminated obesity development in February 2007. The earlier positive signal from the smaller 12-week study was never confirmed.

After 2007, a different sponsor, Lateral Pharma, carried the peptide forward under the name LAT8881. It was later studied in trials for neuropathic pain, acute migraine and lumbar radicular pain. Those studies are not summarised here, as they fall outside AOD9604's metabolic research history.

sections.heading: AOD9604 Side Effects: What Human Studies Reported
body: Published human safety data on AOD9604 are limited to the sponsor's six historical trials, summarised in one pooled 2013 paper. Headache was the most frequently reported adverse event, at rates similar to placebo. At the highest oral dose in a short 7-day study, participants reported diarrhoea and flatulence more often. In one intravenous study, a small number of participants reported euphoria. Across the trials, IGF-1 levels and glucose tolerance did not differ meaningfully from placebo, and no anti-AOD9604 antibodies were detected.
These findings describe a specific clinical-grade material given under trial supervision. They should not be read as describing the safety of any unspecified current research lot.

sections.heading: Preclinical Evidence
body: Most of the early positive signal for AOD9604 comes from obese rodents. These findings describe what researchers observed in those models. They are not evidence of an effect in people, and the largest human trial did not reproduce them.

rows: Body-weight gain reduced by more than half vs control; higher adipose lipolytic activity; insulin sensitivity unchanged
Obese and lean mice, chronic dosing
Less weight gain and more fat oxidation in obese mice; no GH-receptor binding or cell proliferation in vitro
Chronic weight and lipolysis effects absent, though an acute rise in energy expenditure still occurred
Cartilage-repair outcomes reported, alone and combined with hyaluronic acid

after_table: A related peptide, AOD9401, was studied separately in some of the same rodent models; those results belong to AOD9401, not AOD9604.

sections.heading: What the Evidence Does Not Establish
list: That AOD9604 causes weight or fat loss in humans, given the null result of the largest efficacy trial
Safety or efficacy for subcutaneous or topical use, since no published human data cover those routes
Cartilage or joint repair in humans; that evidence is animal-only
Anything about the identity, purity or content of a specific vial, which requires lot-specific testing

problem_solution.title: Confirming AOD9604 identity across sources
problem_solution.problem: Vendor listings use AOD9604, AOD-9604 and hGH Fragment 176-191 somewhat interchangeably, and they do not always describe the same peptide.
problem_solution.solution: Confirm identity from sequence, disulfide state and expected mass together, cross-checked against a lot-specific analytical result, rather than from the product name alone.

problem_solution.title: Telling a molecule reference apart from a lot result
problem_solution.problem: A correct formula and molecular weight on a product page say nothing about what is in a specific vial.
problem_solution.solution: Treat PubChem-level identity data and a lot's certificate of analysis as two different things. Confirm purity and content only from the certificate that matches that lot.

problem_solution.title: Reading animal findings alongside human results
problem_solution.problem: Rodent weight-loss findings and the human trial outcome are easy to blend into one impression.
problem_solution.solution: Keep the two separate. Preclinical work reported metabolic effects in obese rodents, while the largest human efficacy trial did not find a significant weight-loss benefit over placebo.

problem_solution.title: Interpreting mechanism language
problem_solution.problem: Terms such as 'stimulates lipolysis' can read as a demonstrated effect rather than an observation.
problem_solution.solution: AOD9604's molecular target has not been established, so treat mechanism findings from specific cell and animal models as context, not as proof of a confirmed pathway.

problem_solution.title: What 'AOD9604 benefits' searches actually lead to
problem_solution.problem: Search interest in AOD9604 benefits often points to promotional summaries rather than trial data.
problem_solution.solution: The relevant research is a set of preclinical metabolic findings and a human trial programme whose primary efficacy result was not significant; that is what the evidence supports.

problem_solution.title: Reading historical trial protocols without using them as instructions
problem_solution.problem: Clinical trial dose levels and schedules can look like usage guidance.
problem_solution.solution: Trial design, route and population are described here for context only. Veracue does not provide dosing, reconstitution or administration guidance for any product.

problem_solution.title: Why a purity percentage alone is not enough
problem_solution.problem: A single purity number does not confirm what a peptide is or how much is actually in a vial.
problem_solution.solution: Look for a named method such as HPLC, a mass spectrometry result consistent with the expected species, a matching lot number, and the stated salt or counterion form.

problem_solution.title: Distinguishing AOD9604 from related sequences
problem_solution.problem: AOD9604, native hGH 176-191 and AOD9401 are closely related but distinct peptides, and findings for one are sometimes applied to another.
problem_solution.solution: Match on the printed sequence: AOD9604 begins Tyr-Leu-Arg..., native hGH 176-191 begins Phe-Leu-Arg..., and AOD9401 is a separate analogue studied in its own set of papers.

sections.heading: Reading an AOD9604 Certificate of Analysis
body: Veracue's public certificate library did not include an AOD9604 certificate of analysis at the time of writing. To request lot documentation for a specific order, contact the Veracue team.

A useful AOD9604 COA confirms what the material is, how pure it is by a named method, and that the report belongs to the lot in hand. Look for the peptide name and sequence, plus a lot number matching the vial. It should also give purity by a named method such as HPLC, a mass spectrometry result stated against an expected value, and the testing laboratory and test date.

For reference, the free base has a monoisotopic mass of about 1813.86 Da. A salt form will weigh more, so the COA should state which form was tested. This is reference information only, not a result from any specific lot.

sections.heading: Storage and Handling
body: Store this material according to the conditions on its lot documentation and label, and handle it as a laboratory chemical with appropriate personal protective equipment.

sections.heading: Research Use Only Notice
body: AOD9604 supplied by Veracue is intended solely for laboratory research. It is not a drug, dietary supplement, food or cosmetic, and it is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease. It must not be administered to humans or animals.

The scientific information on this page summarises published research and is not medical advice or a statement of efficacy or safety. Purchasers are responsible for using the material lawfully and in an appropriate research setting. See the Medical Disclaimer for more detail.

faq.question: What is AOD9604?
faq.answer: AOD9604 is a synthetic 16-amino-acid peptide built from residues 177–191 of human growth hormone, with an added tyrosine at the N-terminus and one internal disulfide bond. Metabolic Pharmaceuticals developed it as a potential oral obesity drug in the 1990s and later studied it under the code LAT8881. Veracue supplies it for laboratory research only.

faq.question: What is the sequence of AOD9604?
faq.answer: YLRIVQCRSVEGSCGF (Tyr-Leu-Arg-Ile-Val-Gln-Cys-Arg-Ser-Val-Glu-Gly-Ser-Cys-Gly-Phe), with a disulfide bond linking the cysteines at positions 7 and 14. That bond closes part of the chain into a loop.

faq.question: What is the molecular weight of AOD9604?
faq.answer: The free base has the molecular formula C78H123N23O23S2, an average molecular weight of 1815.1 g/mol, and a monoisotopic mass of about 1813.86 Da. Salt forms weigh more, so always check which form a given document describes.

faq.question: Is AOD9604 the same as hGH Fragment 176-191?
faq.answer: Not quite, though the names are often used interchangeably. Native hGH residues 176–191 begin with phenylalanine (FLRIVQCRSVEGSCGF). AOD9604 instead adds a tyrosine ahead of residues 177–191 (YLRIVQCRSVEGSCGF). Many vendors list the tyrosine sequence under the 176-191 name, so a certificate's sequence is a more reliable guide than the product name alone.

faq.question: Does AOD9604 stimulate growth hormone release?
faq.answer: The cited research does not establish that. AOD9604 is a short fragment derived from the C-terminal end of hGH, not intact growth hormone. It did not compete with hGH for receptor binding in vitro. In human trials, serum IGF-1 did not differ from placebo, which is consistent with it not acting as a conventional GH secretagogue.

faq.question: What did AOD9604 human trials show?
faq.answer: Six sponsor-funded trials tested AOD9604 in about 900 adults between 2001 and 2006, mostly with oral dosing. The early studies focused on safety and tolerability. The largest, a 24-week Phase 2B trial called OPTIONS, tested efficacy directly and did not find a statistically significant weight-loss benefit over placebo.

faq.question: Did the Phase 2B AOD9604 trial show significant weight loss?
faq.answer: No. The OPTIONS study enrolled 536 adults with obesity and compared oral AOD9604 with placebo over 24 weeks alongside a supervised diet and exercise programme. The sponsor reported that weight loss versus placebo did not reach statistical significance at either the 12- or 24-week analysis, and it ended the obesity programme in February 2007. An earlier, smaller 12-week study had reported a positive signal in a conference abstract, but that result was never supported by full published data.

faq.question: What side effects were reported in AOD9604 studies?
faq.answer: Headache was the most common adverse event across the trials, at rates similar to placebo. Diarrhoea and flatulence appeared more often at the highest oral dose in one short study, and a small number of participants reported euphoria during intravenous dosing. These findings come from historical clinical-grade material given under trial conditions, so they describe that programme, not any current research-grade lot.

faq.question: Is AOD9604 FDA approved?
faq.answer: No. AOD-9604 is not an FDA-approved drug. In a 2024 evaluation, FDA weighed the available evidence against including AOD-9604-related substances on the 503A Bulks List used for pharmacy compounding. It cited incomplete characterisation and limited effectiveness and safety data.

faq.question: What should an AOD9604 certificate of analysis include?
faq.answer: A useful COA names the peptide and its sequence, gives a lot number matching the vial, and reports purity by a named method such as HPLC. It should also give a mass spectrometry result consistent with the stated form, near 1813.86 Da monoisotopic for the free base. The testing laboratory and test date should appear too.

faq.question: Does Veracue provide AOD9604 dosing information?
faq.answer: No. Veracue does not publish dosing, reconstitution or administration guidance for any product. Historical trial doses are described only where needed to explain study design, and they are not usage instructions.

faq.question: Are there AOD9604 before-and-after results?
faq.answer: No controlled data show a reliable individual effect. The human results are group averages from placebo-controlled trials, and the largest trial found no significant difference from placebo. Veracue does not publish transformation images or testimonials.
